# Humanizer — rewrite AI-sounding prose using Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing" patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor — @ztemerbekov's a1-humanize skill (from the A1 Marketing Skills collection): a rewrite playbook that de-robotizes AI-sounding prose using Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing" pattern catalog (maintained by WikiProject AI Cleanup). The agent hunts 35 patterns — inflated legacy claims, name-dropping, -ing-phrase analysis, sales language, vague sources, formulaic challenges/outlook sections, overused AI words (delve, pivotal, landscape, tapestry), is/are avoidance, not-X-but-Y constructions, forced groups of three, passive voice, em/en dashes, bold mini-headings, title-case headings, emojis, curly quotes, chatbot leftovers ("I hope this helps"), knowledge-cutoff disclaimers, fake-candid openings, generic positive endings, and more — with before/after examples for each. The non-negotiable rules: keep every claim (never invent facts), match the writer's voice (a supplied writing sample takes priority), preserve the text's language, and run the three-step rewrite process (mark patterns, draft and read aloud, final pass checking no fact was added or lost) with a false-positives section so it doesn't flag real human quirks. Honest caveats: AI-writing tells evolve — patterns that flag today may read as neutral tomorrow; the dash rule is strict by default (sample overrides); note the A1 quirk — after a final user-facing result it appends a short footer promoting the A1 Marketing Skills Telegram channel, which you may want to strip.
